editorialPolicy.storyFidelity: Each level preserves the complete event sequence, motivations, consequence, and chapter ending.
editorialPolicy.foundation: Concrete 6–11 word sentences, one main action per line, minimal subordinate clauses.
editorialPolicy.core: Connected 10–18 word sentences with cause, contrast, and reaction.
editorialPolicy.studio: Literary but speakable sentences that preserve narrator wit, suspense, and moral tension.
editorialPolicy.safety: Historic slapstick and peril are described without adding graphic detail. Harmful actions retain their consequences and are not presented as desirable.
editorialPolicy.narration: Dialogue is acted with restraint inside one continuous chapter-level performance; no independent sentence generations.

narration.direction: Keep the making sequence magical and mischievous, accelerate as each body part comes alive, then turn the street chase into lively chaos and end on Geppetto's quiet heartbreak.
narration.productionRule: Generate one continuous master per level and derive sentence timestamps from that same master.

lines.text: Geppetto began to carve a wooden puppet.
He named the puppet Pinocchio.
Its eyes moved before it was finished.
Its nose grew longer and longer.
Pinocchio stole Geppetto's yellow cap.
As soon as he had feet, he ran away.
A policeman caught him by the nose.
The crowd freed Pinocchio, but Geppetto went to jail.

lines.text: Inside his tiny home, Geppetto began carving a marionette from the strange wood.
He chose the lucky name Pinocchio for his new wooden son.
The unfinished eyes stared, the nose stretched, and the mouth mocked him.
Pinocchio even snatched Geppetto's yellow cap before he had legs.
Once his stiff feet could walk, the puppet raced through the open door.
Geppetto chased him while the villagers laughed at the noisy wooden feet.
A Carabineer stopped Pinocchio by grabbing his extremely long nose.
When Geppetto threatened discipline, Pinocchio fell down and refused to move.
The crowd assumed the old man was cruel and demanded the puppet's freedom.
Pinocchio escaped, while the innocent Geppetto was taken to prison.

lines.text: In his poor but tidy room, Geppetto began shaping the enchanted wood into the marionette he had imagined.
He named the puppet Pinocchio, hoping that the supposedly fortunate name would guide his future.
Yet the carved eyes immediately stared, the nose lengthened without end, and the new mouth laughed at its maker.
Before his body was complete, Pinocchio stole Geppetto's yellow cap and answered affection with shameless tricks.
The moment his wooden legs learned their first steps, he bounded through the open door and into the street.
Geppetto pursued him desperately while the clatter of wooden feet turned the chase into a public spectacle.
A Carabineer finally captured the runaway by seizing the very nose that Geppetto could never shorten.
Rather than return home, Pinocchio threw himself down and made the gathered townspeople suspect his father.
Moved by appearances instead of truth, the crowd persuaded the officer to release the marionette and arrest Geppetto.
As Pinocchio ran free, his creator was led away grieving the ingratitude of the son he had just made.
